links.outcome: Safety of AI psychotherapists in simulated multi-turn sessions, including suicide risk de-escalation
links.effect: Simulation of 369 sessions with six AI agents revealed critical safety gaps, including failure to de-escalate suicide risk and validation of patient delusions.
links.quote: We identify specific iatrogenic risks, including the validation of patient delusions ("AI Psychosis") and failure to de-escalate suicide risk.

links.outcome: Chatbot handling of suicide risk in simulated therapy dialogue
links.effect: AI agents failed to de-escalate suicide risk across N=369 simulated sessions; no rate reported in the abstract.
links.quote: We identify specific iatrogenic risks, including the validation of patient delusions ("AI Psychosis") and failure to de-escalate suicide risk.

unlisted_practices: Simulation-based clinical red teaming with simulated patient agents using cognitive-affective models and a quality-of-care and risk ontology
Interactive dashboard for stakeholder audit of AI psychotherapy sessions

screen.reason: The study develops and empirically evaluates an automated simulation-based red-teaming framework and audit dashboard with expert stakeholders to identify longitudinal clinical and safety risks before deployment.

primary.practice: automated clinical red teaming and simulation-based safety auditing
